finding.claim: SQL injection in ORDER BY: the unvalidated `sort` GET parameter is concatenated directly into the query. Attacker can inject arbitrary SQL, e.g. subqueries/CASE expressions for boolean/blind extraction of data from any table in the SQLite DB (stacked queries are not available via query(), but UNION is not possible after ORDER BY; blind/conditional ordering works).
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) at list.php:6

trace.note: string concatenated into SQL and executed via PDO::query

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, casting, or escaping in list_users_sorted. Contrast: list_users_safe (line 10-11) uses an allowlist and find_user (line 16-17) uses a prepared statement; both are safe. No authentication/authorization checks exist in the file.

verdict.reason: list.php:5-6 concatenates $_GET['sort'] straight into PDO::query with no allowlist, cast or escaping, so the sink is real. But list_users_sorted is never called anywhere in the directory (grep finds only the definition at list.php:4), and requesting list.php directly only defines functions. Whether an unauthenticated attacker can reach it depends on code outside this directory.

verdict_facts.reason: list.php:5-6 takes $_GET['sort'] and concatenates it into the ORDER BY clause of a PDO::query() call with no allowlist, cast or escaping; the allowlist at list.php:10-11 is only in list_users_safe, a different function.
